hf.description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 leaderboard submissions (Harbor job folders with ATIF trajectories and agent session logs)

s3.description: SWE-bench leaderboard submission trajectories (swe-bench/experiments metadata.yaml assets -> public S3 bucket swe-bench-submissions)
s3.licence: none declared (no LICENSE file in swe-bench/experiments; public bucket, read-only; only aggregates are derived and nothing is redistributed)

PubCallsN.desc: LLM calls in the sampled trajectories

PubClaudeCodeSharePct.desc: cache-read share, Claude Code on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (public)

PubScaffoldsCachingN.desc: distinct scaffolds among the caching systems

PubShareMaxPct.desc: highest cache-read share of input, caching systems

PubShareMedianPct.desc: median cache-read share of input across caching systems

PubShareMinPct.desc: lowest cache-read share of input, caching systems

PubSystemsCachingN.desc: public systems (scaffold x model) with caching in use

PubSystemsNoCacheN.desc: public systems with no cache reads recorded (not used or not reported)

PubTrajectoriesN.desc: sampled public trajectories with at least one call

notes: Composition only: benchmark runs have no human idle pauses, so nothing here bears on idle expiry of cache entries.

input = uncached + cache read + cache write (as in the paper); share = read / input. Where a scaffold records no separate write (ATIF, OpenAI-style usage) the write stays inside prompt_tokens, so input and the share are unaffected but uncached and write are merged.

Scaffolds differ in caching configuration (explicit cache_control placement, provider automatic caching, proxies); systems with no read field are 'not_reported' and systems whose reads are all zero are 'not_used'; neither is a 0% data point.

Sampling: 50 units per system drawn with random.Random('<seed>:<system id>').sample over the sorted unit list (seed 2027); a unit is one SWE-bench instance trajectory or one Terminal-Bench trial (task x attempt).

System = one leaderboard submission (scaffold x model); several share a scaffold. declared_model is the submission's stated model; models lists the model field of the recorded responses (they can differ, e.g. a litellm alias, and Claude Code also calls a small model).

sources.command: python tools/public_trajectories.py fetch --data <dir> --n 50 --seed 2027 && python tools/public_trajectories.py build --data <dir>
sources.description: Per-call usage recorded in publicly released agent trajectories: Terminal-Bench 2.0 leaderboard submissions (Harbor job folders with ATIF trajectories and agent session logs) (https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/terminal-bench-2-leaderboard, harborframework/terminal-bench-2-leaderboard@572b2614be2c0cb2527e14f5b1e4026f1072e6c1, licence: apache-2.0 (dataset card)); SWE-bench leaderboard submission trajectories (swe-bench/experiments metadata.yaml assets -> public S3 bucket swe-bench-submissions) (https://github.com/swe-bench/experiments, swe-bench/experiments@40f164d5b8f1d249bf95a6df8b74b577fd8e519d; S3 objects pinned by sha256, licence: none declared (no LICENSE file in swe-bench/experiments; public bucket, read-only; only aggregates are derived and nothing is redistributed)). sha256 is over the sorted '<path> TAB <sha256>' list of every sampled file.
